Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B)=\frac{1}{5},$ the **exact** area of $△ABC$ shown above is{{field-1}} square units.
worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B)=\frac{1}{5}.$ Notice that relative to $∠B,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{AC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B) & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ \frac{1}{5} & =\frac{6x-1}{15x} \\ 15x & =5(6x-1) \\ 15x & =30x-5 \\ 15x & =5 \\ x & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =15x=15(\frac{1}{3})=5, \\ AC & =6x-1=6(\frac{1}{3})-1=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 5\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
